note: The same six options and defaults, as booleans.

Forge's own ECMA-48 pattern: CSI, OSC/DCS/SOS/PM/APC strings and two-byte ESC sequences. It removes more than CyberChef's pattern, which leaves operating-system command strings (a window title), character set selections and the single-character escapes in place.
Starts with a lower case letter and counts letters only, as CyberChef does; adds a first parameter to start upper.

Only letters with a case are varied (at most 12, so at most 4,096 lines) instead of every character: CyberChef writes the same line several times for a character without a case. The first letter varies fastest, all lower case first, as CyberChef's; the delimiter is a choice.

Forge's own pattern tokenizer: every plain letter becomes [xX] with the lower case first, as CyberChef's ([hH] for h and for H); classes and ASCII letter ranges gain the other case ([a-f] becomes [a-fA-F]), where CyberChef nests brackets inside a class; letters beyond ASCII (an e with an accent) are covered too, escapes, group names and quantifiers are copied.

The inverse of case:to-insensitive-regex: a class with both cases of a letter becomes the first one, so [hH] is h as in CyberChef. A class that holds one plain letter ([b]) loses its brackets, and the second case in bigger classes is dropped ([a-zA-Z0-9] is [a-z0-9]).

The delimiter is the shared choice list, none (nothing between the characters) by default as in CyberChef, whose delimiter is free text. A backwards range (z-a) is E_RANGE where CyberChef gives nothing, ranges may not exceed 65,536 code points, and \- and \\ are the only escapes.
Named remove (drop is a core word).

Forge's escaper, written in FL, follows the rules of the library CyberChef uses, found by comparing outputs over every level, quote, JSON, ES6 and upper-case combination: levels special, everything and minimal; quote single, double or backtick; the short escapes \b \t \n \f \r, \0 (not before a digit), \xHH, \uHHHH, \u{H}, the vertical tab as \x0b, and with JSON on the chosen quote put around the text. Forge text is made of Unicode scalar values, so a lone surrogate cannot occur.

Reads the single-letter escapes (also \a, the bell), \xHH, \uHHHH (and surrogate pairs), \u{H} and octal; an unknown escape is kept as written. Forge also reads \` and \/ (so unescape inverts escape at every level), and a lone surrogate or a value above U+10FFFF is E_COERCE where CyberChef writes the surrogate.

Modes string, regex and extended (the escapes \n, \t, \x41 of the pattern are read first, which is CyberChef's Extended mode) plus an ignore-case flag. The pattern may not be empty (CyberChef counts 0).

Units byte and bit as CyberChef, plus char (a code point); input raw or hex. Raw text is compared as UTF-8 bytes (CyberChef compares UTF-16 characters), samples of different length are E_COERCE, as in CyberChef, and so are hex samples with an odd number of digits or a non-hex digit (CyberChef reads them leniently).

Over code points (CyberChef counts UTF-16 characters, so a character beyond the BMP costs 2 there); the dynamic programme is a private primitive (limit 100 million cells). Costs for insertion, deletion and substitution, as CyberChef.

A text report instead of highlighted HTML: one row per matching line with a score, the matched positions and the line, scored by a documented greedy rule rather than CyberChef's Sublime-style matcher.
A text report instead of highlighting: one row per stretch of offsets where all samples share the same character (offset, length, text).
